body:
On macOS, a Herdr server started from a terminal tab stayed inside that terminal app's launchd job and resource coalition, even after `setsid`. Quitting the terminal (a plain Cmd-Q of Ghostty, or a force quit) removed that job and killed the server outright with every pane; only the saved layout came back as fresh shells.

The autostarted server now goes through launchd: it is submitted as a one-shot job in the user's GUI domain (own coalition, never restarted), and the job process immediately forks the real server and exits, so the server is not a running GUI job at logout and keeps the lifetime a directly spawned server had. Starts over SSH, or commands launchd cannot carry byte-for-byte, keep the old direct spawn. The job description is written to a private `mkdtemp` directory and removed right away; finished launcher jobs are cleaned up later. Panes keep the caller's umask and do not see launchd's job name.

refs #4920

Validation:
- reproduced on macOS 27.0.1 + Ghostty 1.3.1: Cmd-Q of the everyday Ghostty kills a server started from its tab (no shutdown log); with this change the server and a running pane survive Cmd-Q, live handoff keeps panes outside the terminal's coalition, `herdr server stop` stops without restart
- new macOS tests: a detached child stays in the caller's coalition (the bug), the launchd job gets its own coalition and is not restarted, private temp file permissions, plist escaping/rejection, stale job selection
- `just check` on Linux; macOS module tests on a real GUI session
- not tested: an actual macOS logout; privacy (TCC) prompts may now name herdr instead of the terminal
title: fix: keep the macos server running when its terminal quits
